summary: New York lawyer Roy Cohn helped send the Rosenbergs to the electric chair, drove McCarthy's Red and Lavender Scare purges, then became a mob lawyer and fixer who mentored Donald Trump before dying of AIDS in 1986.

evidence.note: Cohn's birth in the Bronx in 1927 into a wealthy political family
joins the US Attorney's office; Rosenberg prosecution in 1951 starts the main span
vivid account of Ethel Rosenberg's botched electrocution
Cohn becomes Hoover's channel for planting damaging stories in the press
long Lavender Scare segment: Cohn leads interrogations of suspected gay employees
Schine draft and the Army investigation that ends McCarthyism
Cohn as lawyer and business partner for Fat Tony Salerno and the mob
meets Trump in 1973 over the housing discrimination suit; teaches counterattack tactics
yacht sinking, insurance payout and a sailor's death
Trump Tower concrete deal with New York mob-controlled unions
1980 Reagan campaign work and Roger Stone dirty tricks with the Liberal Party
disbarment, failed AIDS treatment and death in 1986

notes: Primary theme is a judgment call: part 1 is mostly McCarthyism (moral-panics, anti-lgbtq), part 2 mob and political fixing; electoral-politics chosen for the fixer/Trump pitch. reaches_present for recurring discussion of Trump and Stone using his methods up to 2020. Antisemitic scapegoating of his uncle and Trump's housing bias get a few minutes each; racism left out.
